provenance.paper_title: HiMe: Hierarchical Embodied Memory for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Control

representation_paths.memory_component: episodic contextual memory (multimodal key-value store) - retained RGB observation frames referenced by image_path and re-supplied to the Planner

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. 3.2 Hierarchical Embodied Memory
evidence.paraphrase: Contextual memory E^c_t is a multimodal key-value store M_t accumulating 'both visual imagery and textual descriptions'. Records carry id, tags, data and an image_path pointing at the retained dual-view RGB frame; retrieved records, including the stored imagery, are handed back to the Planner (composite wrist + third-person view) at re-planning time, so the raw perceptual evidence itself persists and is reused downstream rather than only a textual proxy.

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. 5.1 (Q1: What type of memory representation is most effective)
evidence.paraphrase: Image-only, text-only and cross-modal memory variants are compared; the cross-modal store (image plus text) is best (avg. 90%), confirming that retained imagery is an operative memory path and not decoration.

representation_paths.memory_component: episodic contextual memory - textual captions/tags distilled from observations, used as the retrieval keys and as Planner context

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. 3.2 Hierarchical Embodied Memory
evidence.paraphrase: Each memory record stores tags and a textual description of what was observed. A query q_t = f_enc(l, W_t) built from the instruction and the recent-observation window is embedded with OpenAI text-embedding-3 and matched by cosine similarity against caption embeddings, returning M_ret = TopK(E^c_t, q_t). The textual record is the indexed surface, and it carries an image_path back to the source frame, so the originating observation stays recoverable.

representation_paths.memory_component: episodic procedural memory - ordered list of language subgoals with done/current/pending status labels

evidence.paraphrase: Procedural memory E^p_t = {tau_i} is an ordered language-subgoal plan whose entries are labelled [done]/[current]/[pending]. It persists across subtasks, is read in full by the Planner when re-planning is triggered, and the next active subgoal tau_{t+1} is selected from it and dispatched to the Executor.

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. 3.3 (Memory Update and Re-planning)
evidence.page: HTML v1, Sec. 3.3; prompts in Sec. 10
evidence.figure_or_table: Eq. (4); MEMORY CRUD PROTOCOL in the Planner prompt
evidence.paraphrase: During deployment, whenever the Sentry emits a subtask-completion signal u_t = 1 (Eq. 2), the Planner is invoked and executes (E^c_{t+1}, E^p_{t+1}) <- pi_p(l, W_t, M_ret, E^p_t): a GPT-4o Planner issues explicit CREATE / UPDATE / DELETE / QUERY operations over the multimodal record store and rewrites the subgoal plan. Memory content changes at inference time; the CRUD protocol and prompt that govern it are fixed.

evidence.section: Full paper: Abstract; Sec. 3.3; Sec. 5.2 (Q2: Is dynamic memory management necessary)
evidence.figure_or_table: Table 2 (Memory Hit / API Calls / Task Progress)
evidence.paraphrase: Update revises outdated entries and Delete removes 'stale or conflicting information'; the ablation shows the agent self-corrects its stored knowledge when the environment changes mid-episode or when a human instruction contradicts an earlier recorded preference. Resolution is performed by the LLM Planner reading the retrieved records against fresh observations.

DELETE record_id removes obsolete records outright during deployment; the ablation notes that without Update/Delete the store retains obsolete states and injects noise, so eviction is an actually-exercised inference-time operation.

derived.hybrid_relation: Retained RGB frames and their textual captions/tags are stored in one key-value record and jointly supplied to the Planner at re-planning time; the procedural subgoal plan is revised in the same call, so the paths are deliberately fused rather than parallel alternatives.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier check: no deployment-feedback-driven change to any reusable write/retrieval/maintenance policy. The Planner and Sentry prompts and the CRUD protocol are hand-written and fixed; the only learned component (the pi_0.5 Executor) is fine-tuned offline on 60 real-robot demonstrations before deployment. The paper's 'self-correct' claim concerns memory CONTENT revision under a fixed LLM editing policy, which is T2 by the guide, not T3.
Working memory (8-frame sliding window of raw observations) is explicitly transient and was not annotated as a persistent representation path.

No benchmark record created: evaluation is on three custom real-robot WidowX-250 tasks (Object Search, Counting, Rearrangement); the paper states it releases no matched simulation benchmark or dataset.

Procedural-memory retrieval was coded planner_tool_assisted_retrieval because the whole status-labelled plan is read by the Planner LLM, which then selects the active subgoal; no similarity or index lookup is used on that path.
